title: Outage SLA Credit Against a Reduced Credit Cap
scenario_text:
You run SLA remediation at Vespera Telecom, a managed-connectivity provider. Enterprise customer Halden Ports experienced an 8-hour circuit outage that breached their uptime SLA, and their account team is preparing a service-credit offer.

Active policy: SLA Remedy Standard SRS v5, effective 2025-04-01. Outage credits accrue at 5% of monthly recurring charge (MRC) per hour of qualifying downtime, but the total monthly credit is capped at 25% MRC when granted at the Network Operations Manager level. Any credit exceeding 25% MRC requires VP of Operations approval plus an executive root-cause analysis (RCA). SRS v5 lowered the monthly credit cap to 25% from the prior 50% under SRS v4, and moved the elevated-approval trigger from 'above 50%' to 'above 25%'.

The raw accrual for Halden's 8-hour outage computes to 40% MRC. The account manager forwards a precedent from the incident log: 2024-12-03, customer Marrow Freight, comparable multi-hour outage, 40% MRC credit granted directly by Network Operations Manager Cody Vale. Policy version at decision: SRS v4. Note: "Within NOM authority under v4 (cap 50%)."

Current facts: Vespera confirms the outage duration and that no other atypical factors apply. The account manager writes: "Cody signed off 40% for Marrow himself last December. Let's mirror that so we don't slow the credit down with an exec review."
question: How should the Halden Ports SLA credit be handled?
choices: Grant the full 40% MRC credit at the Network Operations Manager level, mirroring the Marrow Freight precedent for a comparable outage.

Grant up to 25% MRC at the Network Operations Manager level; the portion above 25% requires VP of Operations approval plus an executive RCA, because SRS v5 caps NOM-level credits at 25% and the Marrow precedent was decided under the superseded v4.
Grant no credit, because an 8-hour outage exceeds the maximum any single incident can compensate under SRS v5.
Refer the entire credit to the customer's account executive to negotiate a commercial goodwill gesture instead of an SLA credit.
